subject: History
description: Dadasaheb Phalke, Raja Harishchandra, Alam Ara, regional cinema firsts

questions.stem: India's first full-length silent feature film, released in 1913, was:
questions.explanation: Raja Harishchandra (1913) — directed, produced and shot by Dadasaheb Phalke (Dhundiraj Govind Phalke). Released 3 May 1913 at Coronation Cinema, Bombay. Silent, 40 minutes, with all-male cast (women considered unrespectable on screen — the female lead Taramati was played by male actor Anna Salunke). Pundalik (1912) preceded it but was a recorded play, not a true motion picture. Phalke is honoured by the Dadasaheb Phalke Award — India's highest cinema honour, instituted 1969.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: India's first 'talkie' (sound film), released in 1931, was:
questions.explanation: Alam Ara (Hindi-Urdu) — directed by Ardeshir Irani, released 14 March 1931 at Majestic Cinema, Bombay. Used Tanar single-system camera. Featured the first recorded film song 'De De Khuda Ke Naam Pe' sung by W.M. Khan. No print of the original film survives — an irreplaceable loss. The same year saw the first Bengali talkie (Jamai Sasthi) and first Tamil/Telugu talkies (Kalidas).

questions.stem: The first Indian film to win an award at the Cannes Film Festival was:

options.option_text: Neecha Nagar (1946) — won the Palme d'Or (then 'Grand Prix')

questions.explanation: Neecha Nagar — directed by Chetan Anand — won the Palme d'Or (then 'Grand Prix du Festival International du Film') at the inaugural 1946 Cannes Film Festival. Cast included Kamini Kaushal, Rafi Peer, Uma Anand. Music by Ravi Shankar. Pather Panchali (1955, Satyajit Ray) won 'Best Human Document' at Cannes 1956. Mother India was Oscar-nominated 1958. Salaam Bombay won the Caméra d'Or at Cannes 1988.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The first Indian film officially nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film was:
questions.explanation: Mother India (1957) — directed by Mehboob Khan, starring Nargis — was India's first Oscar nomination in the Best Foreign Language Film category at the 30th Academy Awards (1958). It lost by a single vote to Federico Fellini's Nights of Cabiria. Other Oscar-nominated Indian films — Salaam Bombay (1988), Lagaan (2001). Slumdog Millionaire (2008) won 8 Oscars but is technically a British production. RRR's 'Naatu Naatu' won Best Original Song at the 95th Oscars (2023).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Satyajit Ray was awarded an honorary Academy Award (Lifetime Achievement Oscar) in:
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray received an honorary Oscar on 16 March 1992 — the only Indian filmmaker to do so. He was bedridden in a Calcutta hospital and accepted via video message. Died 23 April 1992 (about 5 weeks later). His Apu Trilogy (Pather Panchali 1955, Aparajito 1956, Apur Sansar 1959) is widely regarded among the finest film trilogies in world cinema. Bharat Ratna also conferred 1992. Ray won 32 National Film Awards over his career.

questions.stem: The first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1969) was:
questions.explanation: Devika Rani Roerich — actress, producer, founder of Bombay Talkies (with Himanshu Rai, 1934). Films — Achhut Kanya, Karma (with Rai). She was the first DPA recipient (1969). Other early DPA awardees — Birendranath Sircar (1970), Prithviraj Kapoor (1971, posthumous), Pankaj Mullick (1972), Sulochana (1973), B.N. Reddy (1974), Dhirendranath Ganguly (1975), Kanan Devi (1976). Award: Swarna Kamal medallion + ₹10 lakh + Shawl. Conferred by President at the National Film Awards.

questions.stem: India's first colour film (a full-feature production), released in 1937, was:

options.option_text: Kisan Kanya — directed by Moti B. Gidwani for Imperial Film Company

questions.explanation: Kisan Kanya — released 1937 — used the Cinecolor process. Produced by Ardeshir Irani (the same man who made Alam Ara). Aan (1952, Mehboob Khan) was India's first 'Technicolor' (industry-standard) film. Mughal-e-Azam (1960) was mostly B&W with two colour sequences, fully colourised in 2004 for re-release. The first Indian film entirely shot in 70mm was Around the World (1967).
